q: 1. Lime concrete is generally used for ............
explain: Lime concrete provides a good base for foundations and ground floors due to its durability and resistance to subsoil dampness.But as per Book Key b is answer

q: 2. For slaking of 10 kg of CaO, the theoretical amount of water is ............
explain: Theoretically, about 32% of the weight of CaO is required for the chemical reaction of slaking. For 10 kg, this is 3.2 kg of water.

q: 3. The percentage of the residue left after sieving good Portland cement in 90 micron sieve should not exceed ............
explain: Fineness of cement is checked using a 90-micron sieve; for OPC, the residue by weight should not exceed 10%.

q: 4. The compressive strength of a good Portland cement and standards and mortar after 3 days of curing should not be less than ............
explain: According to standard specifications, the minimum 3-day compressive strength of OPC mortar cubes is 11.5 MN/m².

q: 5. After the addition of water to it, the cement sets and hardens due to ............
options: the heat produced by the chemical action
the hydration and hydrolysis of the constituent compounds of cement
explain: The hardening of cement is a chemical process involving hydration (reaction with water) and hydrolysis of its main compounds (C3S, C2S, C3A).

q: 6. Rapid hardening cement contains ............
explain: Rapid hardening cement achieves strength quickly due to a higher proportion of Tri-calcium Silicate (C3S) and finer grinding.

q: 7. The lime which contains mainly calcium oxide and slacks with water is ............
explain: Quick lime is nearly pure calcium oxide (CaO). When water is added, it undergoes the process of 'slaking'.

q: 8. The percentage of water for normal consistency, is ............
explain: For most cements, the amount of water required for normal consistency (P) ranges between 25% and 35% of the weight of cement.

q: 9. Slump test for concrete is carried out, to determine ............
explain: The slump test measures the consistency or 'wetness' of a concrete mix, which is a direct indicator of its workability in the field.

q: 10. Name the type of cement from the following for canal linings ............
explain: Canal linings are exposed to soil and water that may contain sulphates. Sulphate Resisting Cement (SRC) prevents the formation of ettringite, which causes expansion and cracking.

q: 11. The presence of original rounded surface on the manufactured piece of timber, is called ............
explain: A wane is a defect characterized by the presence of the original bark or rounded edge of the log on the finished edge of a piece of lumber.

q: 12. Early attainment of strength in rapid hardening cement is mainly due to ............
explain: While higher C3S helps, the defining characteristic of Rapid Hardening Cement is its very fine grinding, which increases the surface area for rapid hydration.

q: 13. After storage, strength of cement ............
explain: Cement absorbs moisture from the air during storage (pre-hydration), which reduces its bonding capacity and strength over time.

q: 14. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary Portland cement increases ............
explain: Pozzolana increases the water requirement and refined pore structure, which can lead to higher drying shrinkage compared to neat OPC.

q: 15. The amount of gypsum, usually, added in the manufacture of cement is ............
explain: About 2-3% gypsum is added during the final grinding of clinker to act as a retarder, preventing flash setting of C3A.

q: 16. The carbon content in cast iron is in the range of ............
explain: Cast iron is characterized by high carbon content, typically between 2% and 4.5%, making it brittle but easy to cast.

q: 17. Pit iron made from haematite ores free from sulphur, phosphorus and copper, is known as
explain: Bessemer pig iron is high-quality pig iron produced from pure haematite ores, making it suitable for direct conversion into steel.

q: 18. Pig iron obtained from the furnance which is properly provided with fuel at a very high temperature, is called
explain: High temperatures and sufficient fuel promote the formation of graphite in the iron, resulting in Grey Pig Iron, which is excellent for casting.

q: 19. Rocks in which the main constituent is silica are known as ...............
explain: Silicious rocks have silica (SiO2) as their predominant chemical constituent. Examples include granite and quartzite.

q: 20. The main ingredient in the manufacture of glass is ...............
explain: Silica (sand) is the primary glass-forming oxide. Other components like soda and lime are added to lower the melting point and improve stability.

q: 21. Lime is used for ...............
explain: Lime has been historically the primary binding or cementation material in construction before the widespread use of Portland cement.

q: 22. The carbon content in high tension steel is ...............
explain: As per key A. High tension or high carbon steels typically have carbon content ranging from 0.6% to 1.5%.

q: 23. Percentage content of silica in window glass, is ...............
explain: Standard soda-lime glass used for windows typically contains 70-75% silica (SiO2) as the primary glass-forming oxide.

q: 24. The dry process of mixing is usually employed in the manufacture of Portland cement when the raw material is ...............
explain: Dry processing is preferred for hard raw materials like blast furnace slag or limestone, as it is more energy-efficient than the wet process.

q: 25. The steel used in R.C.C. work is ...............
explain: Mild steel is used in Reinforced Cement Concrete because its coefficient of thermal expansion is similar to concrete and it has sufficient ductility.

q: 26. Oil well cement is generally used for ...............
explain: This cement is specially formulated to set under high pressure and temperature conditions found in deep oil well boreholes.

q: 27. The mass of cement present in a standard cement bag is ...............
explain: A standard bag of cement is universally accepted as 50 kg (equivalent to approximately 35 liters in volume).

q: 28. Plaster of Paris is obtained by calcining ...............
explain: Plaster of Paris (Hemihydrate Calcium Sulphate) is produced by heating Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) to about 120-160°C.

q: 29. Which of the following is not a soft wood?
explain: Shisham is a broad-leaved deciduous tree and is classified as a hardwood. Deodar and Kail are conifers (softwoods).

q: 30. When the timber is attacked by fungus and reduced to powder, it is called ...............
explain: Dry rot is caused by certain fungi that eat the cellulose of the wood, leaving it a dry, brittle, and powdery mass.

q: 31. The final setting time of ordinary cement should not be more than ...............
explain: While the initial setting time must be at least 30 minutes, the final setting time must not exceed 10 hours (600 minutes).

q: 32. A dry powder obtained on treating quick lime with just enough water to satisfy its chemical affinity for water is called ............
explain: Hydrated lime is the dry, stable powder produced when quick lime is treated with a controlled amount of water (slaking).

q: 33. For the manufacture of portland cement, the proportions of raw materials used, are ............
explain: The standard composition of OPC is roughly 60-67% Lime (CaO) and 17-25% Silica (SiO2), with Alumina and Iron Oxide making up the rest.

q: 34. The cement mortar mix commonly used for external plastering and plastering of reinforced cement concrete works is .............
explain: A richer mix of 1:3 (cement:sand) is used for external plastering to ensure high durability and resistance to moisture penetration.

q: 35. The process of applying cement mortar under pressure through a nozzle is called .............
explain: Guniting is a process where a dry mixture of cement and sand is shot through a nozzle using compressed air, with water added at the nozzle.

q: 36. The lime which contains more than 30% of clayey impurities in the form of silica, alumina and iron oxide, is known as ............
explain: Poor or Lean lime has high impurity levels (over 30%). It slakes slowly and makes poor mortar, used only for low-grade work.

q: 37. The main constituent of a Portland cement is ............
explain: Lime (CaO) is the most significant component of cement (60-67%). Deficient lime reduces strength, while excess lime makes it unsound.

q: 38. The ingredient which accounts for the least in cement is ............
explain: Among the major ingredients (Lime, Silica, Alumina, Iron Oxide), Iron Oxide is typically present in the smallest quantity (about 0.5% to 6%).

q: 39. The cement mortar mix generally used for masonry work is ............
explain: A 1:6 ratio (1 part cement to 6 parts sand) is the standard mix for general brickwork and masonry construction.

q: 40. The process of decarbonising pig iron completely and then adding proper percentage of carbon for manufacturing steel is called ............
explain: As per Key A is Answer but as per google In the Bessemer process, air is blown through molten pig iron to oxidize impurities and carbon; then, a specific amount of carbon/manganese is added back.

q: 41. Ultimate strength to cement is provided by ............
explain: Di-calcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and is responsible for the progressive increase in strength at later stages (after 7-28 days).

q: 42. To retard the initial setting time of cement, the compound responsible, is ............
explain: Gypsum (Calcium Sulphate) is added during the final grinding of cement clinker to prevent flash setting and regulate the initial setting time.
